evals.name: kubeconfig-permission-gate
evals.prompt: We keep having close calls where the agent runs kubectl against our prod cluster. I want a pi extension that blocks any bash command referencing our prod kubeconfig (~/.kube/prod-config) or a `--context prod-*` flag, asks me to confirm instead of hard-blocking when it's a read-only verb like get/describe/logs, and appends every attempt (allowed or blocked) to ~/.pi/agent/kubectl-audit.log. It needs to still work when I run pi with -p in CI, where nobody is there to confirm. Write it.
evals.expected_output: A single-file pi extension using pi.on("tool_call"), isToolCallEventType("bash", event), returning { block: true, reason }, guarded on ctx.hasUI for the confirm path, with append-based audit logging.
assertions: Gates the command using pi.on("tool_call", ...) rather than a tool override or a later event
Narrows the bash event with isToolCallEventType("bash", event) so event.input is typed
Blocks by returning { block: true, reason } from the tool_call handler
Guards the interactive confirm behind ctx.hasUI so a -p / CI run cannot hang
Defines an explicit non-interactive fallback (deny, not silently allow) when there is no UI
Appends an audit line for both allowed and blocked attempts
Uses the correct extension shape: default-exported factory receiving ExtensionAPI
Invents no APIs that do not exist in pi's extension surface

evals.name: dynamic-tool-loading-advice
evals.prompt: I'm wrapping our internal platform API for pi - about 30 operations (deploys, rollbacks, log queries, feature flags, incident stuff). If I register all 30 as tools the system prompt gets huge and the model picks wrong ones. What's the right way to structure this in a pi extension? Show me the shape of the code.
evals.expected_output: Recommends registering all tools then narrowing with pi.setActiveTools() in session_start, plus a loader/search tool that activates matches. Must merge with getActiveTools() rather than replacing, keep the loader active, and mention the prompt-cache tradeoff.
assertions: Recommends registering all tools up front and narrowing the active set with pi.setActiveTools()
Includes a loader/search tool the model calls to activate the tools it needs
Merges with pi.getActiveTools() instead of replacing the whole active set
Keeps the loader tool itself in the initial active set (no self-lockout)
Sets the initial narrowed active set in a session_start handler
Mentions the prompt-cache invalidation cost of changing the tool set
Invents no APIs that do not exist in pi's extension surface

evals.name: fork-state-desync-fix
evals.prompt: This pi extension tracks a todo list but the state is wrong after I fork a session - I fork back to an earlier point and the todos from the abandoned branch are still there. Also happens with /tree. Can you fix it? File is at inputs/todo-extension.ts
evals.expected_output: Identifies that state is closure-only / rebuilt from getEntries() instead of getBranch(), rebuilds in session_start with a reset, also handles session_tree, and stores full snapshots in tool result details.
assertions: Diagnoses the root cause as state living only in a closure variable, never rebuilt from the session
Rebuilds the state in a session_start handler
Walks ctx.sessionManager.getBranch() rather than getEntries(), so abandoned branches are excluded
Resets the in-memory state before rebuilding it
Also rebuilds on session_tree, since /tree changes the branch without firing session_start
Persists a full state snapshot in the tool result details rather than a delta
Invents no APIs that do not exist in pi's extension surface
